note: Commerce Invoice adds the commerce_invoice content entity and its commerce_invoice_type bundle config entity to Drupal Commerce. Two invoice types ship: 'default' (Invoice, numberPattern invoice_default) and 'credit_memo' (Credit memo, numberPattern invoice_credit_memo); both use the invoice_default state-machine workflow (states draft, pending, paid, refund_pending, refunded, canceled). Invoice-type config keys: numberPattern, workflow, footerText, paymentTerms, dueDays, logo, sendConfirmation, confirmationBcc, privateSubdirectory. Invoices are created via the commerce_invoice.invoice_generator service (InvoiceGenerator::generate) or automatically by OrderPlacedSubscriber/OrderPaidSubscriber based on per-order-type third-party settings. Medium cases create a known invoice-type config and read a property back; hard cases create an invoice type config entity and verify it against live config. All eval scripts operate on the commerce_invoice_type config entity (no order/node fixtures needed).

evals.prompt: Which invoice types does the Drupal Commerce Invoice module ship with out of the box, and what are their machine names?
evals.expected_output: It ships two commerce_invoice_type bundles: 'default' (labeled Invoice) and 'credit_memo' (labeled Credit memo).

evals.prompt: What are the states of the default invoice workflow (invoice_default) in the Commerce Invoice module?
evals.expected_output: The invoice_default workflow has states draft, pending, paid, refund_pending, refunded and canceled (transitions confirm, pay, refund, cancel).

evals.prompt: In Drupal Commerce Invoice, how do I generate an invoice from an order programmatically? Name the service and method.
evals.expected_output: Use the commerce_invoice.invoice_generator service (Drupal\commerce_invoice\InvoiceGeneratorInterface) and call generate($orders, $store, $profile, $values, $save).

evals.prompt: This Commerce site has an invoice type with machine name 'ci_known'. Inspect the live configuration and give the exact footer text configured on that invoice type.
must_contain_any: Thank you for your business - CIKNOWN
evals.expected_output: The commerce_invoice_type 'ci_known' has footerText 'Thank you for your business - CIKNOWN' (config commerce_invoice.commerce_invoice_type.ci_known).

evals.prompt: This Commerce site has an invoice type with machine name 'ci_known2'. Inspect the live configuration and state which number pattern that invoice type uses.

On this Drupal Commerce site, create a new invoice type with machine name 'ci_proforma' and label 'Pro forma', using the existing 'invoice_default' number pattern and the 'invoice_default' workflow. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create the commerce_invoice_type config entity ci_proforma, e.g. Drupal\commerce_invoice\Entity\InvoiceType::create(['id'=>'ci_proforma','label'=>'Pro forma','numberPattern'=>'invoice_default','workflow'=>'invoice_default'])->save(); (or via /admin/commerce/config/invoice-types/add).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal Commerce site, create an invoice type with machine name 'ci_deposit' (label 'Deposit'), using the invoice_default number pattern and workflow, and set its due days to 14. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create commerce_invoice_type ci_deposit with dueDays set to 14, e.g. InvoiceType::create(['id'=>'ci_deposit','label'=>'Deposit','numberPattern'=>'invoice_default','workflow'=>'invoice_default','dueDays'=>14])->save();
